Recently, Dragonfly Managing Partner Haseeb once again emphasized in an interview an investment principle that seems simple but is extremely difficult to execute: when market sentiment is at its most bearish and the outside world is generally urging people to step aside, what truly matters is not “predicting the bottom,” but “staying in the market.” This view has drawn attention because the crypto market is still in a high-volatility, highly polarized phase, with capital, narratives, and confidence switching rapidly.😐

Haseeb’s remarks are not merely emotional encouragement, but come from hands-on experience as an investor. He said that during periods of industry pressure, he continued to track projects, respond to the market, and maintain his portfolio—reflecting the real day-to-day work of top-tier institutions: great venture investors are not “done once they invest,” but continuously make judgments, provide support, and filter opportunities amid uncertainty.

2、Core Analysis

Haseeb’s core logic can be summarized in two points. First, wealth often comes from exponential growth, and exponential growth typically rewards only those who do not exit midway. Returns in crypto assets are distributed very unevenly: a small number of projects and a few tracks contribute most of the gains. Therefore, if investors fully exit in panic, they often miss the subsequent recovery and breakout phases.

Second, holding steadfast in the market does not mean stubbornly “dead-holding,” but staying sharp in one’s thinking, keeping positions under control, and maintaining a stable pace. Especially in the current market environment, investors need to distinguish “long-term industry value” from “short-term price noise.” Haseeb’s persistence in controversial assets such as Ethereum and Solana is, in essence, not an emotional team-choosing, but a comprehensive judgment based on ecosystem activity, the developer base, network effects, and potential for future expansion.

From an investment approach standpoint, this thinking is closer to “through-cycle allocation.” It requires investors to continue researching and participating during sluggish periods, rather than abandoning the long-term main thesis due to short-term fluctuations. For ordinary users, the most important takeaway is not to copy institutional bets, but to build their own market survival framework: avoid emotion-driven liquidation of positions, and avoid entering only when attention and hype are at their highest.

3、Market Impact and Takeaways

This perspective has three practical implications for the current market. First, institutional discourse is shifting from “chasing hotspots” to “improving survivability,” indicating that the market places greater value on resilience to volatility and long-term building. Second, valuation logic for public chains, infrastructure, and leading ecosystem assets is returning to fundamentals rather than relying solely on short-term narrative. Third, for crypto investors, future wins may depend not only on choosing the right coin, but on whether they can maintain discipline amid extreme volatility.📊

Overall, Haseeb’s viewpoint is not new, but it is especially meaningful in today’s environment. The market never lacks opportunities—the problem is finding people who can stay clear-headed, patient, and action-oriented even in the depths of the downturn. The real gap often isn’t about who has a better understanding; it’s about who can remain at the table during the hardest times.

Haseeb 的表态并非单纯的情绪鼓励，而是来自一线投资者的实战经验。他提到自己在行业承压期仍持续跟踪项目、回应市场、维护组合，这也反映出头部机构的真实工作状态：优秀风投并不是“投完等待”，而是在不确定性中持续做判断、做陪伴、做筛选。

2、核心分析

Haseeb 的核心逻辑可以概括为两点。第一，财富往往来自指数级增长，而指数级增长通常只会奖励那些没有中途离场的人。加密资产的回报分布高度不均，少数项目、少数赛道会贡献大部分收益，因此投资者若在恐慌中完全退出，往往也会错过后续修复与爆发阶段。

第二，坚守市场并不等于盲目死扛，而是保持认知在线、仓位可控、节奏稳定。尤其在近期市场环境下，投资者更需要区分“行业长期价值”与“短期价格噪音”。Haseeb 在以太坊、Solana 等争议资产上的坚持，本质上不是情绪化站队，而是基于生态活跃度、开发者基础、网络效应与未来扩张潜力的综合判断。

从投资方法看，这种思路更接近“穿越周期型配置”。它要求投资者在低迷阶段继续研究、继续参与，而不是因短期波动放弃长期主线。对普通用户来说，最重要的启发不是复制机构押注，而是建立自己的市场生存框架：避免情绪化清仓，避免只在热度最高时入场。

3、市场影响与启示

这一观点对当前市场有三层现实意义。其一，机构话语正在从“追逐热点”转向“提高存活率”，说明市场更重视抗波动能力与长期建设。其二，公链、基础设施和头部生态资产的估值逻辑，正在重新回归基本面，而不是单纯依赖短线叙事。其三，对于币圈投资者而言，未来的胜负可能不只取决于选中哪个币，更取决于能否在剧烈波动中保持纪律。📊

总体看，Haseeb 的观点并不新，但在当前环境下格外有现实意义。市场从不缺机会，缺的是在低谷阶段仍能保持清醒、耐心和行动力的人。真正的差距，往往不是认知高低，而是谁能在最难的时候仍然留在牌桌上。

title: Altcoin Rotation Heats Up While BTC Tests a 3-Year Sentiment Extreme
subTitle:
The Bitcoin profit-to-loss ratio just fell to a 43-month low. Think about that for a moment. Not a 43-day low, not a quarterly blip — forty-three months. That stretches back to the depths many investors have either forgotten or never experienced. And yet today, $BTC sits at $62,523 with a green 24-hour candle of 1.25 percent, while $ETH is up 2.33 percent to $1,758.21. The market is telling two stories at once, and if you only listen to one, you will miss what is actually unfolding.

The first story is the one the headlines are catching. Bitcoin and Ether are extending relief rallies as extreme fear collides with renewed ETF buying, according to CoinMarketCap and Cointelegraph. That phrase — extreme fear meets renewed buying — is the kind of setup that has historically marked inflection points, not continuations. When the crowd is panicking and institutions are quietly accumulating, the asymmetry favors patience. The profit-and-loss ratio at a multi-year low means most recent buyers are underwater. That is not a comfortable place to be, but it is precisely the kind of capitulation-adjacent reading that separates a cycle bottom from a mere dip.

The second story is the altcoin rotation happening underneath the surface. Today's top movers on CoinMarketCap are not small-cap noise — ANSEM surged 100.1 percent, VELVET climbed 32.3 percent, and MAGMA added 28.2 percent. These kinds of violent rotations often appear when capital begins to trickle out of Bitcoin dominance and into riskier corners of the market. It does not mean altseason has arrived. It means the plumbing is being tested. Liquidity is looking for a home beyond the majors, and traders are front-running a potential shift in market structure.

Now, the map that matters. On $BTC, the 72-hour support sits at $58,326 and resistance is pressing at $62,979.86. Current price: $62,523.23. That puts Bitcoin within striking distance of resistance, just $456 away. If buyers can push through and hold above $62,980, the door opens for a momentum continuation toward higher consolidation zones that have not been tested in weeks. If Bitcoin gets rejected here and slips back below that $58,326 support level, the relief rally loses its foundation and the path of least resistance flips back to the downside. That is the line in the sand — tap $BTC on Binance to watch how price reacts to that resistance band in real time.

For $ETH, the picture is arguably more interesting. Support is anchored at $1,565.26 and resistance is at $1,775.78, with the current price of $1,758.21 sitting just below that ceiling. Ether is outperforming Bitcoin on a percentage basis today, and that relative strength is significant during a rotation narrative. If ETH breaks and holds above $1,775.78, it signals that altcoin appetite is broadening beyond isolated pumps — that capital is genuinely rotating, not just speculating. If it fails here and revisits the $1,565 support zone, buyers will need to defend it or risk a deeper pullback that drags sentiment back toward the fear readings we are already seeing. Tap $ETH to track that resistance test directly.

There is also a regulatory angle worth noting. US law enforcement has reportedly dropped its opposition to the CLARITY Act, according to multiple outlets. Legal frameworks moving forward — even slowly — reduce the structural overhang that has kept institutional capital cautious. This does not move prices overnight, but it compounds over cycles. It is the kind of invisible tailwind that only becomes obvious in hindsight.

Here is the broader point. A 43-month low in profit-and-loss ratio, relief rallies led by ETF flows, altcoins posting double-digit gains, and regulatory headwinds softening — all of this happening while fear gauges remain pinned to the floor. The market is not euphoric. It is cautious, fragmented, and under-owned. That is not the profile of a top. It is closer to the profile of accumulation disguised as uncertainty.

The traders making money right now are not chasing ANSEM at plus-100 percent. They are watching the levels that define the next leg — $62,980 on BTC and $1,775 on ETH — and positioning for what happens when those lines either break or reject. The rotation is real, but it is early. The question is whether you are watching the noise or reading the structure.

What do you think — are we seeing the start of a real altcoin rotation, or just another head fake before the next flush?

Not financial advice. Think in cycles, not candles.

The derivatives market just handed us one of the most telling signals we have seen in months, and most retail traders are not paying attention to it.

Bitcoin is trading at $62,513.64 as of this morning, up 1.33% over the last 24 hours on $787.71 million in volume, according to CoinMarketCap. Ethereum sits at $1,756.80, posting a stronger 2.38% gain on $396.29 million in daily volume. On the surface, these look like straightforward relief rallies. Beneath the surface, the derivatives data is telling a much more nuanced story.

Let me break down what funding rates actually measure before we read them. In perpetual futures markets, funding rates are the mechanism that keeps the contract price tethered to the spot price. When the rate is positive, longs pay shorts, meaning bullish leverage is dominant. When it is negative, shorts pay longs, meaning bearish positioning has taken over. The higher the absolute value, the more one-sided the crowd has become, and the more vulnerable that crowd is to a violent unwind.

What makes today's setup interesting is the backdrop. Bitcoin's profit and loss ratio has fallen to a 43-month low, according to CoinMarketCap headlines. That means fewer holders are sitting in profit than at any point since mid-2021. When the majority of the market is underwater, any rally gets sold into quickly because holders are looking to break even. This creates a ceiling effect that derivatives traders exploit by piling into short positions, which in turn pushes funding rates negative.

When funding rates sit deeply negative and then price starts creeping higher anyway, as we are seeing today with $BTC and $ETH, you get a feedback loop. Short sellers who opened positions at lower levels start feeling pressure. If price continues to grind upward toward resistance, those shorts face liquidation cascades that accelerate the move. This is not speculation. It is the mechanical result of how margin and leverage work on every major exchange.

Here is the map that matters for $BTC right now. The 72-hour support sits at $58,326.00 and resistance is at $62,979.86. Current price at $62,513.64 is pressing right against that resistance ceiling. If buyers can push a clean break and sustained hold above $62,979.86, the short squeeze dynamic becomes real, and you could see a rapid move as underwater shorts are forced to cover. If price gets rejected here and falls back toward $58,326.00, that support is the line where dip-buyers have defended before. Holding it again would confirm range-bound behavior. Losing it would signal that bearish momentum is taking control and that the relief rally was nothing more than a dead cat bounce. The level to watch is $62,979.86 on $BTC — tap it to trade the breakout or the rejection.

Ethereum mirrors this tension with tighter parameters. The 72-hour support is $1,565.26 and resistance is $1,775.78. At $1,756.80, ETH is also pressing the upper boundary. A sustained break above $1,775.78 would confirm that the ETF buying momentum cited in today's headlines is translating into real demand, not just headline noise. If $1,756.80 fails to hold and ETH falls back below $1,565.26, it would mean the derivatives market has absorbed the buying pressure and flipped bearish again. Tap $ETH to trade that range.

Meanwhile, the altcoin periphery is showing signs of speculative froth. ANSEM has surged 96.4% and MAGMA is up 25.3% over the same period, according to CoinMarketCap. Moves of this magnitude in low-cap tokens typically appear when derivatives traders close out major asset shorts and rotate capital into higher-risk plays. It is a signal, not a guarantee, that the broader market is shifting from defensive to offensive positioning.

The regulatory backdrop is also evolving in a way that derivatives desks are pricing in. US law enforcement dropping opposition to the CLARITY Act removes a layer of legal uncertainty that had kept institutional flow on the sidelines. For perpetual futures markets specifically, regulatory clarity lowers counterparty risk, which tends to increase open interest over time and draw more sophisticated capital into both $BTC and $ETH contracts.

So what should you actually watch going forward? Open interest changes on $BTC and $ETH perpetuals relative to spot volume. If open interest rises while price pushes toward resistance, that confirms new leveraged longs are entering with conviction. If open interest drops while price holds, it means shorts are closing and spot buyers are stepping in, which is a healthier foundation for any sustained move higher.

The mechanism is the message. Funding rates, liquidation heatmaps, and open interest are not noise. They are the plumbing that determines whether a rally has legs or is built on leverage that will collapse.
